newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Sweden's Landshypotek long-term A.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Sweden's Landshypotek long-term A.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Wednesday it had assigned a long-term A and short-term A1 rating to Sweden's Landshypotek AB.

"IBCA already rates General Mortgage Bank of Sweden (Sveriges Allmanna Hypoteksbank) -- the funding vehicle of the Landshypotek group," the rating agency said. "Landshypotek will undertake new funding in its own name from 1st July 1997."
It said it had assigned the same ratings to Landshypotek as to General Mortgage Bank.

"Landshypotek is the largest supplier of loans to the agricultural sector in Sweden and is owned by Landshypotek ekonomisk foerening (Lef), an "incorporated association" controlled by its members who are Landshypotek's borrowers," IBCA siad.
It said that at present, General Mortgage Bank issues bonds and other debt securities and passes the funds on to Landshypotek on the same terms and conditions.

"Landshypotek and Lef have joint and several liability for General Mortgage Bank's obligations," it said. "From July 1, 1997 Landshypotek will take over responsibility for the group's funding and General Mortgage Bank will be responsible only for managing the run-off of its existing debt."
It said General Mortgage Bank is backed by a 2.3 billion Swedish corwn government guarantee, but said this will not be available to Landshypotek.
" Landshypotek's good performance in 1995 has continued in 1996, and its asset quality and capital adequacy look strong," IBCA said.
"Agriculture has historically been a relatively stable part of the Swedish economy. Landshypotek's market share of loans to Swedish agriculture is around 44 percent."
